own_scenes.desc: Lawrence, Lenny y Lynell Burden, los tres mayores de cinco hermanos, venían del industrial, el new wave y el jazz y quedaron fuera del círculo del Techno Boulevard. Su único contacto, Anthony Shakir, les enseñó a hacer «tracks» en vez de canciones y coló «I Believe» (1990), con la voz de Lisa Newberry y acordes melancólicos, en Techno 2 en lugar de otro tema: un espiritual del techno que eclipsó al supuesto nuevo «Big Fun», «Love Take Me Over» de Area 10. Desde 430 West Eight Mile Road, su sello 430 West acogió a Jay Denham, Eddie Fowlkes o Terrence Parker y ayudó a nacer Seventh City de Daniel Bell y Claude Young (1993).

refs.q: The funny thing is that we used to do full songs, and once we got with Shake we started doing tracks!”
refs.para: Still, Octave One managed to find a way onto the second compilation, courtesy of its only “in”—Detroit techno producer Anthony “Shake” Shakir. As Lawrence Burden recalls, “We met Shake through Terrell Langston, a mutual friend. He [Langston] was doing hip-hop with Shake back then. He used to hear our stuff and he thought it was techno, so he thought we should hook up with Shake. We kinda picked up his vibe a little bit and our sound got smoothed out. The funny thing is that we used to do full songs, and once we got with Shake we started doing tracks!”
